fit_rules.why: No CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md tells agents how this repo works.
Agents that read only AGENTS.md won't see your rules.
Two instruction files; keep one canonical and the other a pointer.
Tests exist, but no CI gate runs them.
No tests detected for agents to verify against.
Some subagents have no tool limits.
A SKILL.md here is over 500 lines.
This repo's settings don't turn on the OS sandbox.

practices.agent_snippet: Keep the skill entrypoint focused; move conditional procedures and references out of the default context when they are not needed for every invocation.
practices.body:
Put the purpose, routing, essential constraints, and the normal workflow in
the entrypoint. Use references or scripts for substantial details that apply
only to a mode, format, provider, or edge case.

The boundary is usefulness, not file size. A short self-contained skill is
better than a router with nothing meaningful to route; a complex skill should
not make every invocation pay for unrelated detail.

## Evidence trail

- [CODEX-SKILL-DESIGN](../../research/sources/codex.md#codex-skill-design): focused skill anatomy and progressive disclosure.
- [CLAUDE-SKILL-SURFACE](../../research/sources/claude-code.md#claude-skill-surface): skills as reusable, on-demand context.
practices.pattern: Keep the skill entrypoint focused and load conditional detail only when the task needs it.
practices.rationale: Lean entrypoints reduce context cost and make the actual operating contract easier to inspect and maintain.
practices.title: Keep skill entrypoints lean

practices.agent_snippet: Describe the capability and its real trigger in the skill description; add an exclusion only when it prevents likely misrouting.
practices.body:
Treat the name and description as a user-facing activation contract. Say what
the skill helps accomplish and the kind of request that should activate it.

Avoid exhaustive keyword lists and broad descriptions that attract unrelated
work. Add a boundary when a neighboring skill or ordinary repository work is
likely to look similar.

## Evidence trail

- [CODEX-SKILL-DESCRIPTION](../../research/sources/codex.md#codex-skill-description): early discovery surface and trigger boundary.
- [CLAUDE-SKILL-DISCOVERY](../../research/sources/claude-code.md#claude-skill-discovery): skill invocation and automatic discovery.
practices.pattern: Describe what a capability does and when it applies without turning its trigger into a catchall.
practices.rationale: Precise triggers reduce accidental activation, missed capabilities, and context spent evaluating unrelated work.
practices.title: Write discriminating skill triggers

practices.agent_snippet: Use skills for reusable reasoning, subagents for isolated specialization, and hooks or CI for behavior that must happen deterministically.
practices.body:
Use a skill when the agent needs reusable knowledge or a reasoning-dependent
workflow. Use a subagent when a specialized or context-heavy task benefits
from isolation. Use a hook, CI check, permission, or approval when the rule
must hold even if the agent misunderstands the instruction.

The boundary is the required guarantee. Do not make a hook carry a long
decision procedure, and do not describe a deterministic safety requirement as
if a prompt alone could enforce it.

## Evidence trail

- [CLAUDE-SKILL-SURFACE](../../research/sources/claude-code.md#claude-skill-surface): extension surfaces and their distinct roles.
- [CLAUDE-HOOKS-DETERMINISM](../../research/sources/claude-code.md#claude-hooks-determinism): skills versus lifecycle hooks.
practices.pattern: Put guidance, isolation, and invariant enforcement in the mechanism designed to provide that guarantee.
practices.rationale: Matching mechanism to guarantee prevents advisory text from being mistaken for enforcement or authorization.
practices.title: Choose the control surface

practices.agent_snippet: Give delegated work only the tools, authority, context, and duration required for its result; isolate repository changes when the task warrants it.
practices.body:
Before delegating, define the result the worker must return and the minimum
capabilities needed to produce it. Restrict tools or permissions, cap an
unbounded loop, and use an isolated worktree when edits should not touch the
parent working copy.

The boundary is proportionality. Read-only research may need broad reading
but no writes; an implementation worker may need edits but not unrelated
external actions. The parent remains responsible for reviewing the result.

## Evidence trail

- [CLAUDE-SUBAGENT-BOUNDARIES](../../research/sources/claude-code.md#claude-subagent-boundaries): subagent capability and isolation controls.
- [CODEX-SKILL-DESIGN](../../research/sources/codex.md#codex-skill-design): preserve scope and do not imply additional permissions.
practices.pattern: Scope delegated agents by capability, authority, duration, and isolation.
practices.rationale: Least privilege and isolation reduce accidental side effects, but the right boundary depends on the repository and the delegated task's risk.
practices.title: Bound delegated work

practices.agent_snippet: After structural validation, exercise a complex skill on representative tasks and revise it from observed routing or decision failures.
practices.body:
Run the package or frontmatter checks first, then decide whether realistic use
would add confidence. For a complex or consequential skill, use representative
tasks to test activation, context loading, permissions, outputs, and failure
boundaries.

Do not confuse a clean parser result with proof that the capability makes good
decisions. Conversely, a tiny self-contained skill does not need a large test
suite merely because it is packaged as a skill.

## Evidence trail

- [CODEX-SKILL-VALIDATION](../../research/sources/codex.md#codex-skill-validation): structural validation versus useful behavior.
- [CLAUDE-SKILL-SURFACE](../../research/sources/claude-code.md#claude-skill-surface): repeated triggers as a signal to revise an extension.
practices.pattern: Validate a reusable capability with realistic use when structural checks cannot show that its decisions are useful.
practices.rationale: Realistic forward use catches routing and decision failures, but a formal behavioral test should match the skill's complexity and consequence.
practices.title: Validate real skill usage

practices.agent_snippet: Route network access from agent-run code through an enforcing proxy and explicit policy — allow, deny, or approve — rather than leaving egress ambient, and confirm a real proxy is in the path before relying on the gate.
practices.body:
Use this when agent-executed code or commands can reach the network. Route egress through an enforcing proxy and an explicit policy — allow, deny, or approve — so exfiltration and untrusted-fetch risk is a mediated decision rather than ambient. A task that genuinely needs the network — installing dependencies, calling a declared API — should get a scoped, explicit grant; the goal is an explicit decision, not a blanket block that pushes people to disable the control. The boundary: this contains egress only where an enforcing proxy is actually in the request path — without one there is nothing to gate — and telemetry recording that a request happened is not the same as a durable audit record.

## Evidence trail

- [CODEX-NETWORK-CAPABILITY](../../research/sources/codex.md#codex-network-capability): the policy decider and execution-scoped proxy that mediate agent network access when managed enforcement is active.
practices.pattern: Treat network access from agent-executed work as a capability mediated by an enforcing proxy and policy — allowed, denied, or routed to approval — not an ambient default of running code.
practices.rationale: Gating network egress through an enforcing proxy and explicit policy — allow, deny, or approve — contains exfiltration and supply-chain risk that ambient network access would leave open.
practices.title: Gate network egress from agent-run work

practices.agent_snippet: Before adding a helper, search the repository for an existing capability and explain why it is insufficient if you add a new abstraction.
practices.body:
Use this when a new helper might overlap existing code. Search symbols, scripts, tests, and nearby modules first; the boundary is crossed only when the search shows a real gap or a materially safer abstraction.

## Evidence trail

- [CODEX-AGENTS-GUIDE](../../research/sources/codex.md#codex-agents-guide): discovery and scoped context sections.
- [CLAUDE-MEMORY-HIERARCHY](../../research/sources/claude-code.md#claude-memory-hierarchy): project and path-scoped instruction sections.
practices.pattern: Search the repository before introducing a helper or parallel abstraction.
practices.rationale: The search-first heuristic prevents duplicate abstractions, but it must allow a new helper when existing capabilities do not meet the requirement.
practices.title: Search before adding helpers

practices.agent_snippet: Keep the change proportional to the requested behavior; separate required refactoring from unrelated cleanup.
practices.body:
Use this when a task touches more than the requested behavior. Include refactoring required for correctness; defer optional cleanup, speculative abstractions, and style migrations so the change remains reviewable.

## Evidence trail

- [CODEX-SKILL-DESIGN](../../research/sources/codex.md#codex-skill-design): scoping work to the task and matching specificity to the risk.
practices.pattern: Keep a change limited to the behavior and evidence needed for the task.
practices.rationale: Narrow scope reduces review and regression risk, but a necessary refactor is appropriate when the requested behavior cannot be correct without it.
practices.title: Make proportional changes

practices.agent_snippet: Produce edits in an explicit, context-anchored format and verify the target context matches before mutating, so a stale or mistargeted change is caught rather than corrupting the file.
practices.body:
Use this when an agent or tool applies edits to files programmatically. Prefer a format that carries surrounding context and is validated against the target before it touches the filesystem, so a hunk that no longer matches is rejected rather than applied blindly. The boundary: parsing a well-formed patch is not proof it applies safely — the context still has to match the current file at apply time. And a full-file rewrite or a structured code transform can be safer than a context patch for large or generated files: match the format to the edit rather than forcing every change through one shape.

## Evidence trail

- [CODEX-PATCH-FORMAT](../../research/sources/codex.md#codex-patch-format): the explicit patch grammar, parsed separately from filesystem application.
practices.pattern: Express an agent-generated edit in an explicit, parseable format with surrounding context.
practices.rationale: An explicit, context-anchored edit format lets the target be checked for a match before mutation, so a stale or mistargeted edit is caught rather than silently corrupting the file.
practices.title: Express edits in an explicit, verifiable format

practices.agent_snippet: Before editing, inspect applicable instructions, repository status, structure, declared commands, and affected paths.
practices.body:
Use this as the first pass on an unfamiliar or changed repository. Learn its local contract—applicable instructions, status, structure, commands, recent changes, and affected paths—before choosing an implementation.

## Evidence trail

- [CODEX-AGENTS-GUIDE](../../research/sources/codex.md#codex-agents-guide): discovery order and nested instructions.
- [CODEX-AGENTS-IMPLEMENTATION](../../research/sources/codex.md#codex-agents-implementation): root detection and candidate ordering.
- [CLAUDE-MEMORY-HIERARCHY](../../research/sources/claude-code.md#claude-memory-hierarchy): instruction hierarchy and path rules.
practices.pattern: Inspect repository structure, instruction files, scripts, and declared checks before acting.
practices.rationale: Orientation prevents agents and humans from inventing incompatible conventions or repeating work already represented in the repository.
practices.title: Inspect the repository first

practices.agent_snippet: Keep durable policy canonical and make agent-specific files thin, discoverable adapters rather than disconnected copies.
practices.body:
Use this when several tools need the same repository guidance. Keep durable policy in one maintained source; adapters may change syntax or scope, but their relationship to that source should stay reviewable.

## Evidence trail

- [CODEX-AGENTS-GUIDE](../../research/sources/codex.md#codex-agents-guide): repository and nested guidance.
- [CLAUDE-MEMORY-HIERARCHY](../../research/sources/claude-code.md#claude-memory-hierarchy): imports and scoped instructions.
- [CLAUDE-ENFORCEMENT-BOUNDARY](../../research/sources/claude-code.md#claude-enforcement-boundary): guidance versus controls.
practices.pattern: Keep durable repository policy canonical and make tool-specific adapters point back to it.
practices.rationale: A discoverable canonical source reduces semantic drift while allowing each tool to receive the syntax and scope it can actually consume.
practices.title: Keep canonical context discoverable

practices.agent_snippet: Test the changed behavior and its plausible failure modes; do not add tests solely to satisfy an arbitrary size threshold.
practices.body:
Use this when deciding whether a small change needs a test. Cover the behavior and plausible failure modes; a file’s size or a numeric threshold is not itself a risk signal.

## Evidence trail

- [CODEX-AGENTS-GUIDE](../../research/sources/codex.md#codex-agents-guide): repository guidance and verification sections.
- [CLAUDE-ENFORCEMENT-BOUNDARY](../../research/sources/claude-code.md#claude-enforcement-boundary): guidance versus enforcement sections.
practices.pattern: Test behavior and risk rather than an arbitrary test-count or line-count target.
practices.rationale: Behavior-focused tests provide stronger evidence than coverage theater while preserving room for judgment on genuinely trivial changes.
practices.title: Test meaningful behavior

practices.agent_snippet: When wiring or registration changes, run the narrowest real-path check that exercises the composition boundary.
practices.body:
Use this when a change affects registration, configuration, imports, routing, or composition. Keep unit tests for local logic, then add the narrowest real-path check that exercises the boundary.

## Evidence trail

- [CODEX-AGENTS-IMPLEMENTATION](../../research/sources/codex.md#codex-agents-implementation): multiple roots and loaded-source provenance.
- [CLAUDE-LOCAL-CONTEXT](../../research/sources/claude-code.md#claude-local-context): nested and imported context.
practices.pattern: Exercise the real call path or integration boundary when wiring is part of the change.
practices.rationale: End-to-end or integration-level evidence catches registration and composition failures that isolated tests cannot see.
practices.title: Test real wiring

practices.agent_snippet: Run the repository's declared verification gate and report exactly what passed, what was skipped, and what remains unverified.
practices.body:
Use this when reporting completion. Find the repository’s declared gate, run the checks relevant to the change, and name any skipped lane; a convenient substitute is not equivalent evidence.

## Evidence trail

- [CODEX-AGENTS-GUIDE](../../research/sources/codex.md#codex-agents-guide): verification sections.
- [CLAUDE-ENFORCEMENT-BOUNDARY](../../research/sources/claude-code.md#claude-enforcement-boundary): hooks and enforcement sections.
practices.pattern: Run the repository's real verification gate before claiming a change is complete.
practices.rationale: A real gate makes evidence repeatable, but the consuming repository must define which checks and human acceptance conditions are authoritative.
practices.title: Use the real verification gate

practices.agent_snippet: Make each completion claim match the evidence lane that actually passed, and name any unverified lane.
practices.body:
Use this when a result could be mistaken for a stronger result. Keep repository inspection, automated checks, deployment evidence, and live acceptance separate, and name the unverified lane.

## Evidence trail

- [CODEX-TRUST-BOUNDARY](../../research/sources/codex.md#codex-trust-boundary): authorization and implementation evidence.
- [CLAUDE-ENFORCEMENT-BOUNDARY](../../research/sources/claude-code.md#claude-enforcement-boundary): guidance and enforcement.
practices.pattern: Describe completion, validation, and acceptance only as strongly as the evidence supports.
practices.rationale: Evidence-scoped reporting prevents false confidence and preserves the distinction between what was inspected, tested, deployed, and accepted.
practices.title: Match claims to evidence

practices.agent_snippet: Before an escalating or irreversible action, compute an explicit allow/ask/reject verdict from policy, profile, and sandbox availability, and route risky writes to approval rather than running them unchecked.
practices.body:
Use this when an agent performs actions with real consequences — writing files, running commands, escaping a sandbox. Compute a verdict (allow, ask, or reject) from explicit policy before acting, so authorization is auditable and risky or non-conforming actions are refused or escalated rather than performed. The boundary: keep the policy narrow and explicit; a decision function that grows to re-encode the whole action's logic has lost the separation it was meant to provide.

## Evidence trail

- [CODEX-SAFETY-POLICY](../../research/sources/codex.md#codex-safety-policy): the three-way safety verdict computed separately from applying the action.
practices.pattern: Compute whether an action is allowed with an explicit policy, separate from the code that performs it.
practices.rationale: Separating the allow, ask, or reject decision from the action makes authorization auditable and lets risky or non-conforming writes route to approval or refusal instead of running unchecked.
practices.title: Decide permission separately from the action

practices.agent_snippet: Run agent-executed commands inside an OS sandbox with least privilege where a supported backend is enabled, surface violations instead of widening the policy silently, and treat "no sandbox available" as fail-safe rather than permission to run unconfined.
practices.body:
Use this when an agent runs shell commands or executes generated code. Confine execution with an operating-system sandbox scoped to least privilege, and treat recorded violations as signal, so a mistaken or malicious command is contained by the platform rather than by trust. The boundary: this holds only where a supported OS backend is available and enabled — platform selection can resolve to no sandbox, and that case must fail safe rather than silently run unconfined. And a sandbox widened until nothing is denied provides no isolation — tighten the policy and surface violations rather than relaxing it to make a task pass.

## Evidence trail

- [CODEX-SANDBOX-ISOLATION](../../research/sources/codex.md#codex-sandbox-isolation): the re-exported platform sandbox managers and violation recorders.
practices.pattern: Run agent-executed commands inside an operating-system sandbox with a least-privilege policy.
practices.rationale: Where a supported OS sandbox backend is enabled, it contains the blast radius of an agent-run command regardless of the agent's intent, and recorded violations make over-broad access visible instead of silent.
practices.title: Confine agent-executed commands in an OS sandbox

skill_repos.install: /plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official, or /plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace then /plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace
skill_repos.name: Superpowers
skill_repos.summary: A development method for coding agents: brainstorm a design, write a plan, then build it through subagents with test-driven development and review gates.
skill_repos.watch_out_for: Its workflows are mandatory by design, and a session-start hook injects the using-superpowers skill into every session. The optional brainstorming visual companion pings the authors' site with your version unless you opt out.

skill_repos.install: /plugin install mattpocock-skills (official marketplace), then run /setup-matt-pocock-skills in each repo
skill_repos.name: Skills For Real Engineers
skill_repos.summary: Skills for everyday work with an agent, built around an interview that pins down the task before any code is written and a shared glossary of your project's domain terms.
skill_repos.watch_out_for: Run /setup-matt-pocock-skills once per repo before the engineering skills; it asks about your issue tracker and edits your CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md. Plugin updates can lag the repo by days or weeks.

skill_repos.install: /plugin marketplace add addyosmani/agent-skills, then /plugin install agent-skills@addy-agent-skills
skill_repos.name: Agent Skills
skill_repos.summary: Twenty-five skills that take a feature from spec and plan through tests, review and launch, with a slash command for each stage.
skill_repos.watch_out_for: The scripts in hooks/ are not wired by the plugin, so you set them up yourself. Installing a single skill with npx leaves out the shared references/ checklists.

skill_repos.name: Web Quality Skills
skill_repos.summary: Web audits for performance, accessibility and SEO that prefer measuring with Lighthouse and DevTools traces before changing code.
skill_repos.watch_out_for: It works best with Chrome DevTools MCP; without it the skills fall back to the Lighthouse CLI or static inspection of the source.

skill_repos.install: /plugin marketplace add wshobson/agents, then /plugin install each plugin you want, e.g. python-development@claude-code-workflows
skill_repos.name: claude-code-workflows
skill_repos.summary: A marketplace of 94 plugins, each covering one area such as Python, code review or security scanning, so you install only what you need.
skill_repos.watch_out_for: Some plugins are outside engineering (marketing, HR, trading). The protect-mcp and review-agent-governance plugins run an npx package from hooks on every tool call.

skill_repos.install: /plugin marketplace add OthmanAdi/planning-with-files, then /plugin install planning-with-files@planning-with-files
skill_repos.name: Planning with Files
skill_repos.summary: Keeps a long task's plan, findings and progress in markdown files and re-injects them through hooks, so the agent can pick the task back up after /clear or context compaction.
skill_repos.watch_out_for: Hooks fire on every prompt and before most tool calls, and an optional gated mode can keep the agent from stopping until every phase is marked complete.

skill_repos.install: /plugin marketplace add jeffallan/claude-skills, then /plugin install fullstack-dev-skills@fullstack-dev-skills
skill_repos.name: fullstack-dev-skills
skill_repos.summary: Sixty-seven specialist skills, each named for a role such as code reviewer or DevOps engineer, across many languages and frameworks. Reference files load only when relevant.
skill_repos.watch_out_for: The marketplace installs from a generated plugin branch, not the main branch reviewed here. The nine project-workflow commands need an Atlassian MCP server and create and update Jira tickets.

skill_repos.install: /plugin marketplace add levnikolaevich/claude-code-skills, then /plugin install each plugin you want, e.g. implementation-suite@levnikolaevich-skills-marketplace
skill_repos.name: Claude-Codex Skills
skill_repos.summary: Skills written as strict checklists that make the agent show evidence before it calls a task done, split into eight plugins from planning to delivery.
skill_repos.watch_out_for: Each skill is long and formal, so context cost is real. The delivery plugin has skills that commit, push, release and deploy; they ask for explicit authorization, but read them before installing.

skill_repos.name: claude-code-java
skill_repos.summary: Eighteen Java skills with depth in Spring Boot, JPA and concurrency review, plus an eval script that checks a prompt reaches the right skill.
skill_repos.watch_out_for: The optional setup scripts write CLAUDE.md, a settings file with pre-approved commands and MCP config into your project, and the routing eval needs a model API key; the skills install without any of it.

skill_repos.install: /plugin marketplace add oliver-kriska/claude-elixir-phoenix, then /plugin install elixir-phoenix
skill_repos.name: Elixir Phoenix Plugin for Claude Code
skill_repos.summary: A plugin for Elixir and Phoenix work, with plan, work, verify and review commands, reviewer agents, and rules against common LiveView and Ecto mistakes.
skill_repos.watch_out_for: Hooks run on edits, prompts and Bash commands, and some deny commands such as mix ecto.reset or force pushes.

skill_repos.install: /plugin marketplace add LukasNiessen/terrashark, then /plugin install terrashark
skill_repos.name: TerraShark
skill_repos.summary: One Terraform and OpenTofu skill that has the agent work out how a change could fail, such as exposing secrets or touching more resources than intended, before it proposes a fix.
skill_repos.watch_out_for: It is one skill plus reference notes with no scripts, so it guides the agent but checks nothing itself.

skill_repos.install: /plugin marketplace add tzachbon/smart-ralph, then /plugin install ralph-specum@smart-ralph
skill_repos.name: Smart Ralph
skill_repos.summary: Spec-first development: the agent writes requirements, design and task files you can review, then works through the tasks one at a time, each in fresh context.
skill_repos.watch_out_for: Its Stop hook keeps the agent going while tasks remain. It commits after each task and can push a feature branch, and quick mode skips the approval stops between phases.

skill_repos.install: /plugin marketplace add cathrynlavery/diagram-design, then /plugin install diagram-design@diagram-design
skill_repos.name: Diagram Design
skill_repos.summary: Draws architecture, sequence and other technical diagrams as self-contained HTML and SVG files, and can redraw existing Mermaid, draw.io or Excalidraw sources in its own style.
skill_repos.watch_out_for: Generated files load Google Fonts when opened, and PNG export needs Playwright and Chromium installed separately.

skill_repos.install: npx skills add Agents365-ai/drawio-skill -g, or git clone the repo to ~/.claude/skills/drawio-skill (also needs the draw.io desktop CLI for exports)
skill_repos.name: drawio-skill
skill_repos.summary: Turns a prompt or existing Terraform, Kubernetes, SQL or OpenAPI files into editable draw.io diagrams, and updates them later without losing layout you arranged by hand.
skill_repos.watch_out_for: Diagrams built from live infrastructure snapshots can carry sensitive values, icons come from CDNs or remote URLs, and the skill bundles about 45 Python scripts.

skill_repos.install: /plugin marketplace add Egonex-AI/Understand-Anything, then /plugin install understand-anything
skill_repos.name: Understand Anything
skill_repos.summary: Builds a browsable knowledge graph of a codebase, so a newcomer can ask questions about it, see what a diff touches and get an onboarding guide.
skill_repos.watch_out_for: The first /understand run on a large repo can use a lot of tokens. Its hooks do nothing until you enable --auto-update, after which they tell the agent to refresh the graph after commits and at session start without asking.

skill_repos.install: /plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail, then /plugin install ponytail@ponytail
skill_repos.name: Ponytail
skill_repos.summary: An always-on prompt that pushes the agent to write less code and reuse what already exists, with a command that reviews a diff for over-engineering.
skill_repos.watch_out_for: Hooks run at session start and on every prompt, keep a flag file under ~/.claude, and once nudge the agent to edit settings.json for a status line.
